newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees lower foreign investment in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees lower foreign investment in 1996.

text.p: Indonesia's Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo predicted approvals for foreign investment would be lower in 1996, but said the country was still attractive to foreign money.

"I think the value of approved foreign investment will be lower this year compared with last year. But the number of projects are higher. Indonesia is still attractive," he told reporters on Saturday.
He said approved foreign investment from January 1 to November 15 was $28.6 billion and covered about 930 projects.
He did not give a comparative figure, but Indonesia's approved foreign investment in 1995 was $39.9 billion for 799 projects.
"Investment realisation is still around 51 percent. We are making efforts to increase the realisation," he said.
He said the projects in the January-November period included agriculture, chemicals, electronics and property.
